items.title: GTA VI Needs To Hit $1.9B In Sales To Meet Investor Expectations, Says BofA –  Analyst Sees 33% Potential Upside In TTWO Stock
items.summary: BofA estimates that GTA VI needs to generate at least $1.9 billion in sales to meet investors’ fiscal 2027 expectations.

items.title: Grand Theft Auto VI Makes Take-Two Stock Look Like a Steal
items.summary: GTA VI could be a cultural moment akin to Taylor Swift’s Eras Tour. This time, investors can buy stock ahead of the actual event.

items.title: Take Two Interactive Software (TTWO) Rallies On GTA VI Buzz, Is The Upside Already Priced In?
items.summary: Take-Two Interactive Software (TTWO) is back in focus after its latest earnings release and a fresh outlook tied to Grand Theft Auto VI. Investors are weighing softer recent results against management’s guidance for a potentially historic fiscal 2027. Over the past few sessions, Take-Two Interactive Software has moved sharply higher, with a 1-day share price return of 2.97% and a 7-day share price return of 10.73% as traders react to GTA VI preorder commentary and upbeat fiscal 2027 guidance...

items.title: JPMorgan names top Mid & Small Cap stock pick
items.summary: Investing.com -- JPMorgan has identified its top stock pick in the mid and small cap sector, highlighting Take-Two Interactive Software as its leading choice as the gaming company prepares for the highly anticipated Grand Theft Auto VI console release.

items.title: Take-Two's Zelnick on Success of the GTA Franchise
items.summary: Take-Two Interactive CEO Strauss Zelnick talks about the highly anticipated release of Grand Theft Auto VI, out next week. He says the Grand Theft Auto franchise "is probably the most valuable intellectual property in the entertainment business" because of its enormous global reach. Zelnick sits down with David Rubenstein on this week's episode of The David Rubenstein Show: Peer to Peer Conversations. This interview was recorded October 19 in New York.

items.title: Take-Two CEO sends strong message to investors ahead of GTA 6
items.summary: Take-Two’s soft quarter didn’t shake its chief. Bank of America set a bar for launch weekend and sees GTA’s long-term payday arriving later than hoped.
